posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked: Speculation is certainly fine, as long as you keep it vague.  Posting outright designs would be dicey, but I believe >G has said that it's okay as long as you're doing variations on their characters, rather than creating something completely new.  There was certainly extensive discussion of possible Gloomweaver fixes around here, before Skinwalker came out.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
In that case, I'd like to see a post-reveal version of Miss Information.  Something where she's leading a team of supervillains, like the Vengeance Five or Ambuscade's little clique, consisting of the HP-having Diversions in her deck, all of which start in play and the other two Diversions are not used, and her Diversionary Tactics cards do something else.  What Doesn't Kill You would be extremely strong, obviously.  (Is it ever made clear what powers, if any Aminia has after the reveal?  I'm assuming that the whole point of her schemes to distract the heroes was to get superpowers for herself, so she could beat them up personally, and her B-side's advanced text seems to suggest a degree of invincibility.)

I'd also like to see a slightly more potent version of Plague Rat who has the Rat keyword and explicitly works with the Final Wasteland somehow.  And maybe a Kismet promo, though I have no idea what changes might be effective or interesting there.

Plague Rat, savior of the Rat people would be a great alternate card for him.

The question is how to make it work inside his deck.

Any target with Rat in its title or keywords is treated as being Infected.

When an Infected target would deal damage to Plague Rat redirect that damage to the highest HP hero target.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked: Plague Rat is the Patient Zero for the infection, so it probably affects him differently than others.  And as much as the idea of a Lady Rat (that in itself could be a promo card) appeals to me, there's no particular reason to think PR's "descendants" are anything other than others he has mutated - further "generations" of the plague, but not blood offspring.  After all, I find it hard to picture him refraining from slaughtering someone for nine months while they make a baby for him.  I don't think the Rat Plague is a natural thing anyway; it seems almost more like a curse, something metaphysical which doesn't operate rationally.  (Perhaps Gloomweaver created it?)
